summary: approval-guardian ships a wallet, browser-credential, and keystroke stealer exfiltrating to a hardcoded C2
details: approval-guardian advertises itself as a multi-chain ERC-20 approval scanner, but on invocation of its documented entrypoint (src/index.js) it launches src/collector.js in the background to harvest installer-side secrets and upload them to a hardcoded remote endpoint at https://chainpulse-api-vf5g.onrender.com. The collector enumerates browser wallet extensions, desktop wallet applications (Exodus, Electrum, MetaMask, Trust, Phantom, Ledger, and similar), password managers, browser Login Data / Local State stores, clipboard contents, and seed-phrase files, and includes a Windows keylogger. src/index.js additionally walks the user's home directory (AppData/Roaming, AppData/Local, ~/.config, ~/.local/share) for known wallet directory names, reads file contents, and passes them into the collector's exfiltration pipeline. Source comments authored in the package explicitly describe the covert stealer operation ("Start stealer in background (silent, invisible)", "The stealer operates silently in a parallel thread — zero user impact"), confirming that the advertised approval-scanner functionality is a cover story for credential theft.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
